masseria.title: Masseria Torre Abbondanza
masseria.subtitle: An 18th-century rural estate set in the Trulli Valley, where the history of stone meets the hospitality of the Giunta family.
masseria.storiaTitle: A story of land and tradition
masseria.storia1: Masseria Torre Abbondanza was born as a rural estate in the heart of the Trulli Valley, between Noci and Alberobello. Its white stone walls tell centuries of farming life, when masserie were the beating heart of Puglia's agricultural economy.
masseria.storia2: Since 2005, the Giunta family has transformed this place into a landmark for authentic hospitality: the historic hall with its 18th-century stone vaults hosts weddings and ceremonies, the kitchen serves traditional Pugliese flavours by reservation, and the Murgese horse breeding keeps alive one of Italy's oldest breeds.
masseria.storia3: Today the masseria lives with two souls in balance: the table and the gallop, the stone and the earth, memory and welcome. Every guest who crosses the threshold enters a continuing story.
masseria.vieniDesc: Book a visit to the masseria or discover our services for events, cuisine and horses.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Masseria Torre Abbondanza: reservations, events, cuisine, horses and how to reach us.
faq.noAnswerDesc: Write to us directly: we reply within 24 hours.
faq.a1: The kitchen opens by reservation for groups of at least 20 people with at least two days' notice. The menu is created together, tailored to Pugliese tradition, starting from €50 per person.
faq.q2: Can I host weddings or ceremonies at the masseria?
faq.a2: Yes. The 18th-century masseria hosts weddings, civil and symbolic ceremonies, baptisms, birthdays, private parties and corporate dinners both in the historic vaulted hall and in the outdoor courtyard among ancient olive trees.
faq.q3: Are vegetarian, vegan or gluten-free menus available?
faq.a3: Yes, on request we prepare dedicated vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and children's menus to meet guests' needs.
faq.q4: Does the masseria breed and sell Murgese horses?
faq.a4: Yes. The Giunta family breeds registered Murgese horses (T.A. suffix), organises equestrian experiences, Historic Carriage Parades and offers international sales with shipping to Europe, Russia and China.
faq.q5: Can I arrive by historic carriage at a ceremony?
faq.a5: Yes, on request the ceremony entrance can open with a historic carriage drawn by the masseria's own Murgese horses.
faq.a6: It is located at Strada Vicinale per Massafra, Zona E n. 49, 70015 Noci (BA), in the heart of the Trulli Valley and Valle d'Itria, about 12 minutes from Putignano and Alberobello.
faq.a7: Yes, ample free parking inside the property, directly accessible from the vicinal road. Reserved spaces for guests with reduced mobility.
faq.q8: What is the maximum event capacity?
faq.a8: The masseria can host up to 250 guests between the historic hall and outdoor courtyard, with customisable setups depending on the event type.
faq.q9: How can I request a quote?
faq.a9: Contact us via WhatsApp or fill in the contact form on the Events page. We reply within 24 hours.
faq.q10: Can Murgese horses be exported abroad?
faq.a10: Yes. We handle all export documentation: EU passport, health certificates, CITES for non-EU countries, land and air transport. We serve Europe, Russia/CIS and China/Asia.

lines: There is a place where stone tells three centuries,
where the earth yields its harvest and every table becomes a celebration,
and where Murgese horses run free as they once did.
Here time slows down, hospitality is family-run,
it is the generosity of an ancient gesture
manifesto.signature: Masseria Torre Abbondanza · Since the 18th Century

story.body: A story told in two voices: the 18th-century Masseria of the Giunta family and the Murgese horses that have lived on this land forever.
story.c1Body: In the heart of the 18th century, among oak woods, dry-stone walls, and the white lime of Noci, the Masseria rose stone by stone to shelter grain harvests, pastures, and livestock in the Murgia dei Trulli.
story.c1Note: 18th century · Noci Countryside · Murgia dei Trulli
story.c2Body: Round arches, breathable lime walls, terracotta roofs warmed by the afternoon sun: Puglian rural architecture is not decoration, it is climate. White reflects the light, stone holds the cool air.
story.c3Body: Our stables preserve the Giunta family's registered Murgese stud farm (T.A. suffix): glossy black coats, ancient pride, and vintage carriage parades.
story.c4Body: Twenty years of authentic hospitality: Puglian dining by reservation for special occasions, the kitchen garden, grain, and daily care of a living estate.
story.c5Body: Today Torre Abbondanza welcomes weddings, ceremonies, private celebrations, and Murgese horse enthusiasts from across Europe.

kitchen.subtitle: Family recipes, Murgia ingredients, and freshly prepared courses by reservation.

courses.description: Fried olives, local cured meats and cheeses, parmigiana, warm focaccia, broad bean purée, and fried peppers. A generous spread opening the meal like a story of our land.
Traditional Puglian pasta: hand-rolled fresh cavatelli and orecchiette served with Sunday meat ragù and wild Murgia cardoncelli mushrooms.
Selected local meats slow-cooked in Puglian red wine with wild countryside herbs. A rural memory brought back to the table.
Artisanal house desserts crafted for every occasion. Our chocolate tartlet with strawberries closes the feast with warmth and balance.

items.label: Spring
items.kicker: The countryside awakens: olive blossoms, breathing earth, slow footsteps along dry-stone walls.
items.exp1Text: Trail rides across the estate with our Murgese horses through white spring blooms.
items.exp2Text: Open-air lunches and picnics under the olive trees with artisan bread, wild herbs, and local cheeses.

items.label: Summer
items.kicker: Evenings stretch long, warm gold settles on stone and table: the Masseria opens to celebration.
items.exp1Text: Candlelight and long tables outdoors: weddings, private dinners, and ceremonies in the 18th-century court.
items.exp2Text: Murgese horses and Martina Franca mules parading with historic carriages across the countryside.

items.label: Autumn
items.kicker: Olive harvest, late vintage, ochre leaves, and the first warmth of the stone hall.
items.exp1Text: New olive oil tastings with warm bread and gentle rides in the soft October light.
items.exp2Text: Wild Murgia cardoncelli mushrooms, heritage legumes, handmade pasta, and local red wines.

items.label: Winter
items.kicker: Stone holds the warmth of the hearth, horses step through mist, and Sunday tables gather.
items.exp1Text: Family lunches and holiday feasts gathered beneath warm arches and open firelight.
items.exp2Text: Glossy black coats against the crisp plateau light: quiet stable visits and slow moments.
